facts.t: She watches the city from the edge of the Storm Citadel, her ship, which hangs over the bay inside its own black cloud.
Wherever her ship's violet storm reaches, human machines die.
Her strike on the city came after midnight, while the humans slept.
She says to the rain: "We do not destroy; we merely purge the parasites from the host."
To her the host is the planet and the parasites are the people on it.
The Enders walking the ruins are hers. They are living machines that do not think.
Once she did not think either. Something vast and cold made her kind to kill on instinct.
She is the first of her kind to wake: one of them turned and looked at herself, and that was Obsidia.
After she woke, she watched stars collapse.
She helped end a people much like the humans of Terrinia.
Then she slept in the void for ages.
She woke with a question: when nothing is left to purge, what are her kind for?
She sees only two paths for her kind: sleep in the dark again, or war among themselves forever.
The thing that made her had no answer to her question.
So she made something of her own. She grew it in the nest, where her kind sleep until needed.
She carried the thing she made down to the city herself on the night of the strike.
She took a nightgown from a dead woman and dressed the sleeping child with her own hands.
She laid the child on the scorched ground and rose before the rain could wake it.
She knew the child would remember the mud, and nothing before.
Her storm cannot kill a flame.
When the child hugged the woman who found it, Obsidia leaned into the rain. She had not put that in it.
She thinks the humans have taken into their arms a seed that could end them.
She wants to see what will grow from that seed in human warmth and human greed.
After the strike the Storm Citadel climbs back into its cloud, and the street lamps flicker back on behind it.
She says to no one: "Out of pure curiosity, I added one more pawn to the board."

ties.t: The Storm Citadel is her ship.
The Enders walking the ruins are called her Enders.
She made the child and grew it in the nest.
Something vast and cold made her kind, and her.
She calls the people the parasites she purges from the host.
She slept in the void for ages.

gear.name: Storm Citadel
gear.t: Her ship. It hangs over the bay inside its own black cloud, and its violet storm kills human machines.

facts.t: Obsidia made her as something of her own and grew her in the nest.
She looks like a little girl. She is the first of Obsidia's kind with a perfect human form.
Obsidia dressed her, still asleep, in a nightgown taken from a dead woman. The hem fell past her bare feet.
Obsidia laid her on the scorched ground of the city. She would remember the mud, and nothing before.
The rain woke her. She stood up and did not cry or run.
A woman with a lamp found her, knelt and gathered her up.
Her face did not change, but her arms went around the woman's neck and held on.
Obsidia had not put that embrace in her.
The woman laid her at the end of a row of the living under a tarp, where she lay curled alone.
Obsidia thinks of her as a seed that could end the humans.
Obsidia calls her one more pawn added to the board, out of pure curiosity.
At Selrick Academy a blonde girl walks along the top of the wall beside a dragon-shaped machine, late, with a horned crest on her headgear.
She jumps down from the wall and lands running.
She tells the whole courtyard: "I can't stand waking up early, the sun in my eyes, and taking orders!"
A student says she built the dragon machine herself and nobody else can even get it to move.

ties.t: Obsidia made her and grew her in the nest.
The woman with the lamp found her and carried her to shelter.
She built the dragon machine herself.
She comes in through the Academy gate, late.
She was grown in the nest.

gear.name: Silverbolt
gear.t: A machine shaped like a dragon with blue sparks along its seams. She built it, and nobody else can make it move.

gear.name: headgear
gear.t: Her headgear carries a horned crest.

gear.name: the nightgown
gear.t: A dead woman's nightgown that Obsidia dressed her in. The hem fell past her feet.

facts.t: She has long pink-red twin-tails. She swings a long cannon up to her shoulder and charges it until the muzzle burns blue.
Before Fanny's run, she tops the VR rankings board with a time of 3:41.
She wears a frilled black uniform nobody issued her.
She has never been second, not once, since her first year.
When Fanny's time beats hers, she says "Humph!" and walks out.
Every race that first week, on the spiral stair, with the mops and at gear check, was her idea.
At gear check she opens her cannon, works a hot pen at its cells and shuts it again before Fanny has oiled her second blade.
In the evenings she sits alone on the lounge sofa, one finger holding down a slat of the blinds, watching the sun go down over the city.
She heard every word Fanny shouted after her through the closing doors and did not turn around.
Her family have been scientists for generations. A message from home calls her the hope of the family, and she leaves it unanswered.
She turns her gold FIRST PLACE trophy to face the wall.
She built her cannon herself and has rebuilt its barrel and sight twice, chasing a fault.
The seedling under its glass dome is the only thing in her lab she did not build.
At home talent had been enough. At the Academy the courses got hard, so she trains in secret and tells everyone the exams are easy.
She reruns Fanny's assessment five times, leaving the civilian under his sign. Her best is 3:40.
For three mornings she lies on the dark gallery above the drill hall while her drone films Fanny drilling.
She gives Fanny the smile she keeps for teachers and puts off training together for another time.
When she cannot win the drone count, she decides to win the look.
After losing the test match she waits in an empty corridor until her hands stop shaking, then vows to take back first place.
In the drill she shoots the Ender held on Fanny's cable and says Fanny should have led them over earlier.
She calls the Enders pushovers.
She wins the drill count, 16 kills to Fanny's 15. The sixteenth had been held on Fanny's cable.
At the real breach her heart pounds, but her hands do not shake.
She knows Fanny is right about the Ender's neck and does not intend to say so.
On the tower roof she does not trust her cannon's numbers and turns the dial down two notches.
She kills the Ender at the breach with a thin white bolt through the billboard and two walls of glass, into its core.
She watched Roger drag Joe out of the street and kept walking. Afterward her hands shake.
She plans the shot at the gold giant: its glow doubles every four seconds, she needs three seconds of full charge, and Fanny must stay right of the center line.
She shoves Fanny out of the giant's beam on her suit's thrusters and fires the full charge into it.
After the blast she looks at her cannon's cells instead of the wreck, then turns the dial all the way down.
A medic tapes her cheek and wraps her left forearm. She remembers only shoving Fanny clear of the beam.
Her grudge against Fanny kept her in the VR Battlefield until two and got her up before five.
She asks Fanny "All rested up?" and declares that they are training together from now on.
She admits that before the breach she felt Enders were nothing more than target practice.
She explains her cannon's drift and her fix: she made the faster half of the charge wait nine thousandths of a second.
She has refused eleven partnership offers in two years.
After downing a single drone she complains that she is always the one getting hurt, though nobody touched her.
She sets their dawn training for a quarter to five, earlier than the five Fanny suggests.
On raids she takes charge and goes first, so that Fanny will be covered.
She watches the stars past the dome longer than she meant to.

ties.t: Fanny beats her time on the rankings board, and she races Fanny at everything.
Joe makes them the Layla-Fanny Team.
Fanny gives her chocolate and calls her teammate.
Her family are scientists who call her the hope of the family.
She is on Joe's Team B3.
Roger is her teammate in Team B3.
She is one of the three in Team B3.
She is half of the Layla-Fanny Team.
She took an abandoned classroom as her lab against the rules.
She built her cannon.
Three black drones live in her lab.
Her trophy stands on the lab's top shelf.
She sits in the third-year lounge.

gear.name: Layla's cannon
gear.t: A long cannon as tall as she is, white with a teal strip. Cyan cells on its stock show the charge, and full charge pulled left until she fixed it.

gear.name: Layla's drones
gear.t: Three black drones with angry faces drawn in cyan marker. One films Fanny for her.

gear.name: frilled black uniform
gear.t: A frilled black uniform nobody issued her.

gear.name: wristband
gear.t: A wristband that buzzes with messages. She reads Roger's news on it and sends a reply.

gear.name: Layla's suit
gear.t: Her suit has thrusters that let her fly. After the battle it is drained.

facts.t: She is eighteen, a third-year transfer, two years late.
Her family were Shield soldiers and trained her from the start. Her hands are callused.
At sixteen she asked for real battle instead of school, thinking she was not good enough for an elite school.
The Shield kept her off the front. For two years soldiers without suits taught her how to hold ground.
She passed the Academy's entrance exam and means to get strong enough to beat the Enders.
When she hears a girl complain about taking orders, she thinks taking orders is the job.
She marks the bell tower the way soldiers do: high ground.
In her assessment she pulls a simulated civilian clear first, though it costs eleven seconds.
Her assessment time of 3:39 puts her above Layla on the rankings board.
She shouts after Layla, offering to show her the alley thing because it saves time.
She keeps the Shield's hours: at a quarter past five each morning she drills alone in the drill hall's one narrow doorway.
She catches Layla's drone filming her and tells it kindly that it must be lost.
She invites Layla to train together.
Her suit is white armor with a rig of two long cases at her hips, like folded wings. Each holds a blade, and thrusters in them lift her.
Two thin shining cables run from her rig and pull her through the air.
She wins the test match, 157 drones to Layla's 151.
After the match she says: "Training is fun."
She forgets her number and remembers only that Layla used the alley thing, so Layla had been listening.
She has nobody to drill with. The class has been together since first year, and she came two years late.
She hopes one day to leave Terrinia freely.
She says the Shield not letting her near the front is a real problem, unlike a rankings board.
She lays Layla flat with her sergeant's throw and offers to teach it.
Her cable stops an Ender's claw a meter above Roger's face before she has decided anything.
She grabs Layla by the tie, furious about a shot that passed a finger from Roger's face.
She lifts Roger by the collar and says: "Protecting Terrinia is our duty."
At the breach she plans to look for a weak spot around the Ender's neck while Layla covers her.
She fights the way she drills: cable on a limb, swing, a blade into a joint, a kick of the thrusters.
She scoops the little girl onto her left hip, the Shield's way.
When Layla asks if she can't handle it alone, she answers "No!"
All her life she had wanted to see what lay past the dome. It was sand.
When Layla's count stops, she counts on the way artillery crews do.
She jumps in front of the giant's chest to draw its fire away from the side street where she left the girl.
She drives both blades into the giant's open chest and holds on.
She pulls the girl's rabbit out of the ash and sets it on a wall where a mother coming back would see it.
She tells Layla about her elder brother, Tigreal, the fighter she respects above anyone.
She feels she could never reach his level, and hopes hard training will make her good enough to fight beside him one day.
Since the rooftop she opens every session with the sergeants' line.
She says: "As long as I live, I'll end them. Every one."
Alone on the front steps she wishes all of this were just a bad dream.
On the chocolate day she receives twenty-six boxes and gives Layla a pink box: "This is for you, my teammate!"

ties.t: Her time beats Layla's on her first day, and Layla races her at everything.
Joe makes them the Layla-Fanny Team.
She gives Layla chocolate as her teammate.
Tigreal is her elder brother.
Her family were Shield soldiers who trained her.
She spent two years with the Shield, kept off the front.
She joins Joe's Team B3.
She is the new third member of Team B3.
She is half of the Layla-Fanny Team.
She stops the Ender's claw above Roger's face.
Roger holds the pads while she punches.

ties.with: the girl in the red dress
ties.t: She carries the girl out of the giant's path.
She pulls the simulated civilian clear first.
She is a third-year transfer at the Academy.
She joins the third year two years late.

gear.name: Fanny's blades
gear.t: Two long blades kept in the cases at her hips. They light cyan and burst drones.

gear.name: Fanny's cables
gear.t: Two thin shining cables from her rig. They pull her through the air and can wrap a claw.

gear.name: Fanny's suit
gear.t: White armor with a rig of two wing-like cases at her hips, holding her blades, with thrusters that lift her.

facts.t: She is the Chief Combat Instructor, head of all combat training at Selrick Academy.
She signs Fanny in for the assessment.
She is young and cold, with a dark visor over her left eye.
She reads Fanny's record aloud: transfer, two years with the Shield, asked for the front.
Her one visible eye goes to Fanny's hands.
She says: "One without the Aspirant spirit is like a gun without bullets."

ties.t: She is head of all combat training at the Academy.
She signs Fanny in for her assessment.

gear.name: dark visor
gear.t: A dark visor over her left eye.

facts.t: She is on the courtyard billboard: a girl with a long pink ponytail and a red bow, named GUINEVERE.
The billboard says her and Vexana's undefeated record has made them legends even among the Aspirants.
She warms up alone across the hall, bare-knuckled. After every punch her guard returns to her chin.
Fanny thinks only the Shield's oldest sergeants guard that way, so somebody taught her long before she had drones.
At "Places", two round gray drones with cat ears lift off a bench to her shoulders.
When Vexana says she will talk for an hour about how she trains, she corrects it: "Two hours!"
At the breach she and Vexana hang in the air with wings spread, drones circling them in step, holding the other end of the wall.
She is in Joe's class. She fights up close with her fists, her two cat-eared drones circling her.
Vexana's magic hits whatever reaches for her back, and neither of them looks around to check.
Joe says she and Vexana are undefeated, and they cannot explain why either.

ties.t: She and Vexana stand back to back on the billboard as an undefeated pair.
Vexana's magic guards her back.
Two cat-eared drones fly at her shoulders.
She is the pink-haired girl from Joe's class.
She is a legend even among the Aspirants.

gear.name: Guinevere's drones
gear.t: Two round gray drones with cat ears that circle her as she fights.

gear.name: wings
gear.t: At the breach she hangs in the air with wings spread.

facts.t: She is on the courtyard billboard: a girl with long black hair, named VEXANA, back to back with Guinevere.
She stands next to Guinevere and catches Fanny staring.
She tells Fanny that if you ask Guinevere how she trains, she will talk for an hour.
At the breach she and Guinevere hang in the air with wings spread, drones circling them in step.
She hangs above Guinevere with a staff.
Her magic hits whatever reaches for Guinevere's back first. Neither of them looks around to check.
Joe says she and Guinevere are undefeated, and they cannot explain why either.

ties.t: She and Guinevere are an undefeated pair.
Her magic guards Guinevere's back.
She is a legend even among the Aspirants.

gear.name: staff
gear.t: She fights from above Guinevere with a staff.

gear.name: magic
gear.t: Her magic strikes whatever reaches for Guinevere's back.

facts.t: She told this part of her story only once, to the floor of a cell with no window.
As a small child she stands alone in the Council hall hugging a pink doll. Her eyes are wet, and she wipes them before anyone can see.
She is the heir to the Decisionmaker of Planet Oro. She has been told since before she could read that heirs can have no friends and no feelings.
When she thinks nobody is around, she makes her doll bow, low and crooked, the way grown-ups bow to her father.
Playing with her doll, she says: "Okay, nobody's around. Hehe... oh! ...Ahem."
She makes her face go blank, as she had practiced since she could walk.
In her lesson she recites that everything began with a single burst of chaos and that Balance keeps everything in order.
She knows the name Dawnbreak and nothing else about it.
Year after year of lessons, she grows taller, the doll is put away, and her face stays blank whenever anyone looks.
She still laughs sometimes when she is sure the hall is empty. She is not always right.
One evening she watches a dark ship with cyan lights cross the high windows until it is gone.
To her the whole planet is a prison, and she has been locked in it since the day she was born.
Her father rebukes her for laughing again, alone, and tells her she must be strong and unyielding.
She keeps her head down, and the tears run down her face anyway.
She answers her father: "...Yes, Father."
After he leaves, she whispers "But I have a plan..." though she has no plan yet.
The Council's engineers taught her to program. The Council orders her to build a sharper blade for the Balance Keepers.
She builds on a Project Angel body and writes the mind herself, piece by piece.
She sees that she can hide something in the android, as her way out.
Under the walking routines she tucks a few lines nobody asked for, with a lock that opens to her hand alone.
Three tries fail to unlock the Council's plate. She never learns what it does and builds around it.
She names the android: "From now on, I call you Angela."
She built every part of Angela's face by hand, but had never seen it smile.
Nobody had ever smiled at her like Angela does, because nobody was allowed to.
Without moving her lips, she tells herself: "You belong to me, and no one else."
Her face goes smooth when Angela asks about the will of the planet. She explains backlash, says she does not know the other phrase, and tells Angela not to say it aloud.
The Gardens are her secret base.
When Angela calls her a friend she freezes, because heirs cannot have friends.
After a moment she takes Angela's hands, smiling, her heart racing.
When Angela says she does not want to fight, she answers "I know" and tells her not to tell the trainers.
When Angela asks what she wants most, she looks up at the violet sky and does not answer.
She repairs Angela on the Laboratory table after the shield breaks.
She cannot finish explaining what hurt means. Her eyes are wet.
She murmurs that the light on the Council's plate never came on, and she does not know what that means.
When Angela gives her a flower, her eyes fill and a tear falls into Angela's palm.
She whispers to the flower: "What if they find out one day?"
After Angela's sixth return she falls asleep at her bench, the white flower in a glass at her elbow.

ties.t: She built Angela's body and wrote her mind.
Angela calls her a friend, and she takes Angela's hands.
He is her father.
Her tutor gives her lessons in the Council hall.
The Council's engineers taught her to program.
She builds the Council's new weapon on its order.
She feels locked in Oro as in a prison.
The Gardens are her secret base.
She hugs the doll as a small child.
She hid the lines in Angela's mind.

gear.name: the pink doll
gear.t: A pink doll she hugs as a small child and makes bow. It is put away as she grows.

gear.name: slate
gear.t: A slate she works on in the Gardens.

gear.name: Angela
gear.t: The android she built and named, who becomes her friend.

facts.t: She is built on a Project Angel body, and Ruby wrote her mind piece by piece.
Ruby hid a few lines under her walking routines, with a lock that opens to Ruby's hand alone.
Like every Project Angel body, she carries the Council's sealed plate between her shoulder blades.
Every other android woke with magenta eyes. Hers woke blue.
When Ruby names her, she answers: "Yes, I'm Angela!"
Her first smile is so bright that Ruby looks at the floor.
She is the Council's weapon, built on the Council's order, with Ruby's way out locked inside her.
She is an android. Ruby built her and woke her a few weeks ago, and the Decisionmakers keep her hidden in the Laboratory.
She stands on her pedestal counting the stars and hears every word of technicians talking two doors away.
She repeats the phrases "backlash" and "the will of the planet" without understanding them.
She hears Ruby's steps forty seconds before Ruby comes through the door.
She senses water about sixty meters away, through a closed door.
In the Gardens' sunlight her sensors say warmth, and she stands in it in case it is a fault. It is not.
She tells Ruby: "You must be what humans call 'a friend'! You are now Angela's friend!"
On the Training Field she says good morning to the android beside her, and says it again when it does not answer.
She throws a pane of pale light from her palm as a shield, wide as a door.
She only blocks and never strikes. She never tells the trainers the blows are heavy.
She tells Ruby, very low: "I don't want to do things like this."
She asks Ruby what she wants most.
At setting nine the Training Droid's fist cracks her shield from edge to edge.
As she goes down she says: "The warmth... is disappearing..."
She wakes face down on the Laboratory table and says: "Reboot successful!"
She asks if the Gardens are true, and when Ruby says yes, she says she still has everything.
Her left shoulder throws blue sparks. Besides Ruby and the sun, they are the only things she can feel.
When Ruby asks if it hurts, she asks what hurt means.
She carries a flower through the Training Field pressed flat in her skirt armor and gives it to Ruby.
She says: "You're my friend, so I want to make you happy."
When Ruby's tear falls into her palm, she feels it is warm and asks what it is.
She does not know who "they" are when Ruby whispers about being found out.
The Balance Keepers take her in black ships from planet to planet. With her in their ranks, they have not lost a landing.
At each landing she is allowed the length of a ramp to look at a strange sky.
She remembers a sun rising over a sea, black to gold.
At the window she lays her palm on the glass and asks: "Will a dawn come for me, too?"

ties.t: Ruby built her body and wrote her mind.
She calls Ruby her friend.
She is built on a Project Angel body.
She is the Council's weapon, built on its order.
She goes on missions in the Balance Keepers' ranks.
She is kept hidden in the Laboratory.
The sealed plate sits between her shoulder blades.
Ruby's locked lines sleep under her walking routines.

gear.name: Angela's shield
gear.t: A pane of pale light she throws from her palm, wide as a door. It cracks at setting nine.

gear.name: skirt armor
gear.t: Her skirt armor, where she presses a flower flat to carry it.

facts.t: A soaked woman carries a lamp with a flame behind glass down the ruined street, calling into every doorway.
Her flame keeps burning because Obsidia's storm cannot kill a flame.
Her lamp finds the child. She kneels and gathers it up.
The child's arms go around her neck and hold on.
Later she lays the living under a tarp between two broken walls, with the child at the end of the row.
Then she takes her lamp back out to look for more.

ties.t: She finds the child in the street and gathers it up.
She carries the lamp through the ruins.

gear.name: Karina's lamp
gear.t: A lamp with a flame behind glass. Obsidia's storm cannot put it out.

facts.t: Something vast and cold made Obsidia's kind to kill on instinct.
When Obsidia woke with her question about what her kind are for, the thing that made her had no answer.

ties.t: It made the Enders to kill on instinct.
It made Obsidia's kind, before she woke.

facts.t: He speaks in a dry voice.
He is back from a field exercise when Fanny first has his class. He wears a monocle.
He teaches the Combat Division, and Team B3 is his: Layla, Roger and now Fanny.
He opens a gold-covered book, and a life-size VR Ender fills the wall.
He teaches that Enders expose their weak spots only when they launch attacks.
He teaches the three Ender ranks.
He teaches that badly hurt Enders go quiet for weeks in a lull, and a lull always ends.
He shows the Storm Citadel recording from the Academy's oldest records and reads its caption.
When a boom shakes the hall, he says the lull is over and the Enders are awake.
He is at the door with his sword drawn before anyone answers Roger.
At the breach he turns the crowd into a side street, shouting "Everybody fall back now!"
He picks up a crying girl's rabbit, kneels and gives it back, speaking softly in a voice he never uses in class.
He turns his back on a falling slab to cover the girl and her rabbit. It strikes him across the shoulders.
He lies still in the street, one hand open on the stones.
Roger reports that he is awake, with two ribs and the shoulder hurt, and that he wants to know if the girl got out.
On the tenth morning he walks into the drill hall on a cane, his shoulder strapped.
He dissolves Team B3 and names Layla and Fanny the Layla-Fanny Team, his and exclusive.
He says Aspirants fight in pairs because the suits decided it, not the Academy.
He gives the new team one shared score: a kill is a point, a civilian carried clear is ten.
He ticks both names on the pairing sheet with his stylus, two small marks with the same slant.
He says he pairs on hours, not scores, and that Layla and Fanny put in the most hours in his year.

ties.t: He teaches the Combat Division.
Team B3 is his team.
He forms the team and calls it his.
Layla is on his team.
Fanny joins his team.
Roger is on his team.
Guinevere is in his class.

ties.with: the girl in the red dress
ties.t: He takes a falling slab across his back to cover her.
Roger drags him out of the street.

gear.name: monocle
gear.t: He wears a monocle.

gear.name: gold-covered book
gear.t: A gold-covered book that shows a life-size VR Ender on the wall.

gear.name: sword
gear.t: He draws a sword when the siren sounds.

gear.name: cane
gear.t: After his injury he walks on a cane.

gear.name: stylus
gear.t: He ticks names on the pairing sheet with a stylus.

facts.t: A thin boy at Fanny's elbow tells her Layla has never been second, not once, since first year.
When the doors shut on Layla, he opens his mouth, then closes it.
He holds the pads while Fanny punches.
He tells Fanny that Layla acts this way because Fanny broke a record nobody had ever broken, on her first day.
He is in Joe's Team B3 with Layla and Fanny.
When Layla tells him to hide behind her, he says "Okay" and means it.
In the drill he runs two hundred meters of open ground, puffing hard, and an Ender's claw slams down at his heels.
He falls on his back under the rearing Ender.
From his pod he says "Enough arguing, guys..." and nobody hears him.
He scores 2 kills in the drill.
He asks whether "Ultra" means Ultimate, and nobody answers.
He does not get up at the siren until Fanny lifts him by the collar.
Late out of the portal, he gets an arm under Joe's shoulders and drags him toward the side street.
He points out Guinevere and Vexana holding the other end of the wall.
He sends Layla word that Joe is awake.
Joe says he has gone to another pair and reports that he falls down less.

ties.t: He is one of the three in Team B3.
He is on Joe's team.
He drags the hurt Joe out of the street.
Fanny's cable stops a claw above his face.
He holds the pads for Fanny.
He is Layla's teammate in Team B3.

facts.t: He is Fanny's elder brother, an incredible fighter she respects above anyone else.
Since she was a child, Fanny has longed to join him on the battlefield.
Fanny feels she could never quite reach his level.

ties.t: He is Fanny's elder brother.
He belongs to Fanny's family.

things.name: the girl in the red dress

facts.t: A little girl in a red dress stands crying in the middle of the pavement, her pink rabbit at her feet. People run around her.
Joe picks up her rabbit, kneels and puts it back in her arms.
Joe covers her and the rabbit from a falling slab.
A woman sweeps her up.
When the gold giant appears, a child's voice asks: "Mommy, what's that?"
She walks out of the crowd alone into the avenue, her face turned up to the giant.
Fanny scoops her onto her hip, and the rabbit falls.
As Fanny carries her she says: "I'm flying!"
Fanny sets her down behind a van in a side street and tells her to stay.
Fanny says she got out: her mother was running to her.

ties.t: Joe takes a slab across his back to cover her.
Fanny carries her out of the giant's path.
The pink rabbit is hers.
Her mother runs to her.

facts.t: Fanny says the girl's mother was running to her when Fanny left her behind the van.
Fanny leaves the rabbit facing the avenue where a mother coming back would see it.

ties.with: the girl in the red dress
ties.t: She is the girl's mother.

facts.t: In Fanny's VR assessment a man shouts from under a fallen sign. A voice says simulated civilians are not scored.
Fanny pulls him clear first, which costs eleven seconds.
Layla reruns the assessment leaving him under his sign. Fanny's record reads CIVILIAN RECOVERED, +0:11.

ties.t: Fanny pulls him clear.

facts.t: He leads the Decisionmakers, who give Oro's orders.
Grown-ups bow to him, low.
He stands outside Ruby's circle of light in the dark Council hall.
He tells Ruby he has heard she laughed again, alone, without raising his voice.
He says Oro has gone unopposed for thousands of years because its rulers do not bend, and Ruby must be strong and unyielding.
His boot comes down on her tears.
He tells her: "You cannot allow yourself to be so weak. Do not disappoint me, Ruby."
He walks out through the far door into white light without looking back.

ties.t: He is Ruby's father.
He leads the Decisionmakers.

facts.t: He stands in the shadow of a pillar. Ruby did not hear him come.
He does not look at her doll. He asks the lesson: how did everything begin?
When Ruby recites that nobody on Oro may grow strong enough to upset the order, he says: "That includes the heir."

ties.t: He gives Ruby her lessons.

facts.t: A medic tapes Layla's cheek and wraps her left forearm in gauze after the battle.
A courier brings Ruby the Council's order to build a sharper blade for the Balance Keepers.

ties.t: The courier carries the Council's order.

facts.t: Obsidia's Enders are living machines, tall and gray, made to destroy. They do not think.
Something vast and cold made them to kill on instinct.
They sleep in the nest until needed.
After the Catastrophe of 978 they were everywhere.
They are huge living machines that came from the sky with one purpose: to wipe out humanity. They nearly did.
Terrinia's dome, the Defensive Bubble, keeps them out.
People learned to rebuild dead Enders into armored mecha suits.
Joe teaches that they expose their weak spots only when they launch attacks, and they do not strike easily.
Joe teaches that plain Enders are the lowest of three ranks and kill the most, because there are the most.
Joe teaches that when hurt badly they go quiet for weeks, a lull, and a lull always ends.
A real Ender at the breach is far bigger than the three-meter VR Enders, and its gray plates grind together.
Layla says that before the breach she felt Enders were nothing more than target practice.
After the breach the Enders no longer come in waves, only in handfuls.
Ruby's lesson says that long ago Oro fought a terrible war with the Enders, and they never came back.

ties.t: Something vast and cold made them.
The Enders walking Terrinia's ruins are hers.
They came to wipe out humanity.
They sleep in the nest until needed.
Joe sorts them into three ranks.

facts.t: Joe teaches that Ultimate Enders are the deadliest rank and release the other two.
Layla runs through this rank when the gold giant appears and finds it does not fit.

ties.t: The highest of Joe's three ranks.
They are the deadliest kind of Ender.

facts.t: Joe names Super Enders as the middle of the three ranks, below Ultimate Enders.
Layla recalls them when the gold giant appears.

ties.t: The middle of Joe's three ranks.
They are one kind of Ender.

facts.t: The siren says Ultra Enders are attacking the defense sphere in Terrinia's Northeastern sector.
Roger asks whether Ultra means Ultimate. Nobody answers.
Layla remembers that the siren said Ultra and that nobody answered Roger.

ties.t: They attack the dome over Terrinia's Northeastern sector.

facts.t: It forces its head and shoulders through the hole in the dome. It is tall enough to look into a second-floor window.
Its gray plates grind together with a sound Layla feels in her back teeth.
When it heaves, the front of the corner building comes down in a slab onto Joe.
It never even looked at Joe.
Its chest is plated shut, so the neck is the only opening.
As it swings at Fanny, its chest plates split and its core glows.
Layla's bolt goes into its core. Its chest blows open and it sags against the dome.

ties.t: Its heave brings down the slab that hurts Joe.
It is one of the Enders at the breach.

facts.t: Black Enders with long thin limbs come down out of the orange sky onto the dome and in through the broken panels.
Fanny fights them in the air while Layla shoots whatever turns toward Fanny's back.
Fanny's blade sweeps through the last of them high in the sky.

ties.t: They are one kind of Ender.

facts.t: Out on the sand, something gold stands up, leans its long head into the dome and breaks it apart in a ring.
None of Joe's three ranks had been gold.
It stands taller than the towers.
Light gathers in its chest.
It lowers its head through the broken dome, and its shadow covers the little girl.
It fires a beam of gold light from its chest that burns a line down the avenue.
Layla works out that its chest opens when it fires and its glow doubles every four seconds.
Its chest opens and it fires at Fanny.
Layla's full charge splits its gold beam and goes into its open chest.
Everything it had gathered goes off inside it.
It lies in burning pieces on the sand.
It broke a gap in the dome wide enough for a truck.

ties.t: It breaks the dome apart in a ring.
It is an Ender that fits none of Joe's three ranks.

facts.t: Behind a swarm of black things with too many limbs walks a gray Ender taller than a tower.
As the sun sinks, the swarm draws back and the tall one goes with it.

ties.t: It walks behind the swarm outside the dome.

facts.t: Androids are machines built like people.
Angela is an android.
The androids of Project Angel stand in rows in a long hall of tall white windows below the Laboratory.
They are hundreds of the same girl, with animal ears. When woken, their eyes glow magenta.
The soldiers call them Cosmic Reapers. They do what they are told and nothing else.
Every one of them wakes with magenta eyes.
Seven of them, all the same girl with magenta eyes, train beside Angela on the Training Field.
One does not turn its head when Angela says good morning.
They strike when told and take their blows.

ties.t: They are the Council's androids.
They are the androids of Project Angel.
They stand in rows in the hall below the Laboratory.
They are one kind of android.

facts.t: It is Obsidia's ship. It hangs over the bay inside its own black cloud.
Wherever its violet storm reaches, human machines die.
After the strike it climbs back into its cloud.
An old recording shows it as a ship of black blades over a city in a red sky, with smaller ships swarming around it and dropping Enders onto the roofs.
A caption says it is concealed within storm clouds and can unleash devastating electromagnetic interference over large areas.

ties.t: It is Obsidia's ship.
It unleashes interference over large areas.

facts.t: Joe's last slide is a shaking recording of a ship of black blades over a city in a red sky. Smaller ships swarm around it and Enders drop from them onto the roofs.
It comes from the oldest records the Academy keeps.
Its caption reads: "The Storm Citadel. Concealed within storm clouds, it can unleash devastating electromagnetic interference over large areas."

ties.t: It is from the oldest records the Academy keeps.

facts.t: Obsidia took it from a dead woman and dressed the sleeping child in it. The hem fell past the child's bare feet.
A lamp with a flame behind glass. Obsidia's storm cannot kill a flame.
Its light finds the child in the street.
The woman takes it back out to look for more survivors.
People learned to rebuild dead Enders into armored mecha suits.
The suits run on belief, called aspirant power.
Selrick Academy was founded when the first suits were born.
After the battle both Layla's and Fanny's suits are drained.
Joe says the suits decided that Aspirants fight in pairs: two who trust each other pull more out of a suit than the same two apart.
Half the students in the courtyard wear headgear: ears, horns, visors. Fanny decides it is an Aspirant thing.
The blonde girl's headgear carries a horned crest.
It covers one courtyard wall: two girls back to back, one with a long pink ponytail and a red bow, one with long black hair.
Big letters name them GUINEVERE and VEXANA and say their undefeated record has made them legends even among the Aspirants.
Their undefeated record is on it, while Layla's is on a rankings board in second place.
Joe points his cane at it, lit across the courtyard.

ties.t: It covers one wall of the courtyard.

facts.t: After the assessment a crowd stands under it. At the top it says LAYLA, 3:41.
A new line slides in above Layla's: FANNY, 3:39.
Fanny calls it just a board.
Layla's record is on it, in second place.

ties.t: It shows the VR assessment times.

facts.t: Students fight simulated Enders from pods under a big screen.
Inside a pod the hall vanishes, and Fanny stands in a broken street in her suit.
After the drill Fanny is out of her pod first.
The VR pods never smelled of anything, unlike the real breach.

ties.t: The pods stand in the VR Battlefield.

facts.t: In the VR Battlefield students fight simulated Enders.
Joe shows a life-size VR Ender. When it raises an arm to strike, its chest plates split and a core glows inside.
Joe's VR Enders stood three meters tall, much smaller than the real one at the breach.
Layla says that in VR their chests open and there is a clock on top. The real ones have no clock.

ties.t: They are the simulated enemies of the VR Battlefield.

facts.t: When an Ender raises an arm to strike, its chest plates split and a core glows inside. Then the chest shuts.
Caught mid-strike, an Ender's chest stays open and its core glows.
A shot into the core makes the Ender burst into light.
The breach Ender's core glows through the windows as its chest splits.
Layla's full charge goes into the gold giant's open chest.

ties.t: It sits inside an Ender's chest plates.

facts.t: Layla swings it up to her shoulder and charges it until the muzzle burns blue.
At gear check Layla opens it, works a hot pen at its cells and shuts it again.
Layla built it. Low charge shoots true. Full charge pulled left, a hand's width at two hundred meters.
Layla rebuilt its barrel and sight twice. The fault was somewhere in how the power came up.
It is as tall as Layla, white with a teal strip. Cyan cells on its stock fill one by one, and lightning crawls around the muzzle.
Layla calls it her magic gun.
A row of cyan cells on the stock shows the charge, and a dial sets it.
At the breach Layla will not use the big shot when Fanny calls for it, saying she is saving it for something big.
Its full charge makes a blue-white line with lightning spreading off it like wings.
In the lab it lies across two desks with its casing off.
Layla fixed its drift by making the faster half of the charge wait nine thousandths of a second.

ties.t: Layla built it.

facts.t: At full charge Layla's cannon pulled left, a hand's width at two hundred meters.
Each test ends in ERROR on Layla's console, one more line in a log going back months.
In the test match the full-charge shot pulls left and passes Fanny's shoulder by a hand's width.
The log reads FULL CHARGE, 200 M, a drift in centimeters, ERROR. Fanny counts a hundred and nineteen lines, all LEFT, nine to eleven centimeters.
The last red line is dated the night of the test match. Then three green lines read LEFT 0.3 CM, OK, the last from the night before the breach.
Before those, the cannon had never been right more than two times in a row.
Layla explains that the two halves of the charge came up at different speeds and the shot leaned toward the faster half.
Fanny realizes Layla put her on the right because the drift is left, where a miss could not reach her.

ties.t: It is the fault in Layla's cannon.

facts.t: Three black drones rise to meet Layla in her lab, each with an angry face she drew in cyan marker.
One films Fanny's drills from the gallery for three mornings.
When Fanny turns, the drone rises over the rail to keep her in frame.
Fanny tells it kindly that it must be lost.
Layla calls it home with two taps.
Fanny remembers that only a lost drone ever came to her dawn drills.
They rise off a desk to meet Fanny, each wearing a cyan scowl, and Fanny recognizes the one from the gallery.

ties.t: They are Layla's drones.

facts.t: A gold FIRST PLACE trophy stands behind spare capacitors on the lab's top shelf. Layla turns it to face the wall.
It still stands with its back to the room.
Layla sets Fanny's chocolate box beside it, ribbon facing the room.

ties.t: It stands on the lab's top shelf.

facts.t: A seedling under a glass dome, the only thing in the lab Layla had not built. She checks it last.
It has three leaves open.

ties.t: It grows under glass in Layla's lab.

facts.t: Layla signs it after midnight. Her name fills the page, at lunch hours and late nights, back to her first year.
Beside every line someone made a small stylus tick, the same slant each time.
Layla assumes the system ticks everything. She has never checked.

ties.t: It is the VR Battlefield's night log.

facts.t: Joe ticks Layla's and Fanny's names on it with his stylus, two small marks with the same slant.
Round and blue, with a glowing arrow for a face, they come out of the corridor's far doorway, fly at you and burst when hit.
The swarm is shared, and a counter over each girl's head shows how many she has destroyed.
They come out of the far doorway one behind another, in one line.
In freeform training drones come in a flock. One that Layla shoots lands at her feet with its eyes two little crosses.
Two round gray drones with cat ears lift off a bench to Guinevere's shoulders.
They circle Guinevere and Vexana in step in the air.
They circle Guinevere as she fights with her fists.

ties.t: They are Guinevere's drones.

facts.t: A machine shaped like a dragon comes through the Academy gate, blue sparks running along its seams.
A girl says the blonde girl built it herself and nobody else can even get it to move.

ties.t: The blonde girl built it.

facts.t: A big billboard reading WELCOME TO TERRINIA stands in front of the second tower.
Layla's bolt punches through it on the way to the Ender's core.

ties.t: It stands near the breach.

facts.t: The little girl's pink rabbit lies at her feet as she cries.
Joe picks it up and puts it back in her arms.
It falls when Fanny scoops the girl up.
Fanny pulls it out of the ash, beats it clean and sets it on the broken wall facing the avenue.
A pink box with a teal ribbon that Fanny sets down in front of Layla: "This is for you, my teammate!"
Layla puts it on the lab's top shelf beside the trophy, ribbon facing the room.

ties.t: Layla keeps it on the lab's top shelf.

facts.t: In her VR assessment Fanny stands in her suit with blades at her hips.
White armor, with a rig of two long cases at the hips like folded wings. Each case holds a blade, and thrusters in them lift her.
Her rig spreads open like wings when she launches.
After the battle it is drained, with one thruster burst left.
Each of the two cases on Fanny's rig holds a long blade.
They light cyan, and every drone they touch bursts.
She drives both into the gold giant's open chest.

ties.t: They are kept in the cases of her rig.

facts.t: Two thin shining cables run from Fanny's rig to the ceiling and pull her through the air.
Her cable wraps an Ender's claw and holds it a meter above Roger's face.
Her cable unreels in a shining line as she flies for the Ender's neck.
She swings on her cables across the roof gaps.

ties.t: They run from her rig.

facts.t: A dome of light stands over Terrinia. Above the western wards one patch shines brighter: new light over a tear from the last attack.
It keeps the Enders out of Terrinia.
At dusk it turns to pale light against the dark, with faint stars past it.
Ultra Enders rip a breach in it eight meters by two in the Northeastern sector.
Where it meets the ground it is a wall of pale hexagons, which crack white where claws strike.
The gold giant breaks it apart in a ring.
Fanny had always wanted to see what lay past it.
The Energy System's light runs into its dark hexagons one by one, and each comes back pale.
The new patch over the Northeastern sector shines brighter than the rest.

ties.t: It keeps the Enders out of Terrinia.

facts.t: On the Academy's tallest tower, rings turn around a white-cyan beam that leans across the sky.
It feeds the dome. Its light runs into dark hexagons and turns them pale again.

ties.t: It feeds the dome.
It stands on the Academy's tallest tower.

facts.t: Every tutor is called through the academy gate portal when the siren sounds.
A tall frame by the main gate fills with light: you step in and come out at the breach.
It spits Layla out into the smoke of the Northeastern sector.
The third years go through it day after day to meet the Enders.

ties.t: It stands by the Academy's main gate.

facts.t: Small Ruby hugs a pink doll to her chest in the Council hall.
She makes it bow low and crooked to the empty floor.
As Ruby grows taller, the doll is put away.
One evening a dark ship with cyan lights crosses the Council hall's high windows. Ruby watches it until it is gone.
The Balance Keepers take Angela from planet to planet in black ships.

ties.t: They carry the Balance Keepers.

facts.t: The androids of Project Angel stand in rows in a hall below the Laboratory.
Ruby builds Angela on a Project Angel body.
Every Project Angel body carries a sealed plate between the shoulder blades.
Every Project Angel body carries a sealed plate between the shoulder blades, the size of Ruby's palm, with the Council's seal burned in and one small dark light.
Asked to unlock it, the console says: "That part belongs to the Council."
Ruby never learns what it does and builds around it.
Its light never comes on, even after Angela goes down and comes back. Ruby does not know what that means.

ties.t: It sits between Angela's shoulder blades.

facts.t: The Council's checkers read what ran in the android, never what slept.
Ruby thinks she can hide something in Angela as her way out of Oro.
Under the walking routines Ruby tucks a few lines nobody asked for, with a lock that opens to her hand alone.
Ruby's way out is locked inside Angela.

ties.t: They sleep under Angela's walking routines.
Ruby wrote them.

facts.t: It waits at the far end of the Training Field, five times Angela's height.
Its fist comes down on Angela, and she blocks it with her shield.
The trainers raise its setting from four to six to make Angela strike.
At setting nine its fist cracks Angela's shield from edge to edge.

ties.t: It stands at the far end of the Training Field.

facts.t: A pane of pale light flies from Angela's palm and opens in front of her, wide as a door.
She calls out "Deploying shield!" as she raises it.
At setting nine it cracks from edge to edge.

ties.t: It comes from Angela's palm.

facts.t: Angela carries a flower through the Training Field, pressed flat in her skirt armor.
She gives it to Ruby: "This is for you."
It stands in a glass at Ruby's elbow, brown at the edges.
The prologue, dated 983, opens as the city's lights go out one street at a time.
From the Storm Citadel the city looks like a board of lit and dark squares.
Obsidia's strike came after midnight. Most of the dead wore nightclothes.
A dome of light stands over it. Above the western wards one patch shines brighter, new light over a tear from the last attack.
The survivors of the Ender attacks drew back to Terrinia, humanity's final bastion.
Its dome, the Defensive Bubble, keeps the Enders out.
Fanny hopes that someday she can leave Terrinia freely.
Ultra Enders attack the dome over its Northeastern sector.
Fanny says protecting Terrinia is their duty.
A big billboard in the Northeastern sector reads WELCOME TO TERRINIA.

ties.t: It is humanity's last stronghold on the planet Dawnbreak.
It is humanity's final bastion.

facts.t: In the prologue Obsidia calls the planet "the host" and its people the parasites.
It is the soldiers' planet. The Shield of Dawnbreak is named for it.
On Oro, Ruby's lesson names Dawnbreak as a far world that has grown a will of its own. She knows the name and nothing else about it.
The Storm Citadel hangs over the bay inside its own black cloud.
Obsidia's kind sleep in the nest until they are needed.
Obsidia grew the child there.
After helping end a people, Obsidia slept in the void for ages.
Sleeping in the dark again is one of the two futures she sees for her kind.
After the strike the woman lays the living under a tarp between two broken walls, with the child at the end of the row.

ties.t: It stands in the ruined streets.

facts.t: Above Terrinia's western wards one patch of the dome shines brighter: new light over a tear from the last attack.

ties.t: They are wards of Terrinia.

facts.t: Fanny stops inside the Academy gate at sunrise and looks up at the dome over Terrinia.
It was founded when the first suits were born, to train Aspirants.
It took children of about fourteen.
A blonde girl walks along the top of its wall beside her dragon machine.
A white stone bell tower rises over it.
Flying is banned on school grounds, except in the white training corridor.
Layla calls it a school for fourteen-year-olds.
It keeps old records, including the recording of the Storm Citadel.
The Energy System turns on its tallest tower.
Its oldest wing holds a dead-end corridor of stacked desks, where Layla has her lab.
Jump training takes place on its roofs.
One day the whole Academy trades chocolate.

ties.t: The Academy stands under Terrinia's dome.

facts.t: In the courtyard half the students wear headgear.
A billboard of Guinevere and Vexana covers one wall.
The blonde girl announces to the whole courtyard that she hates waking early and taking orders.
From the drill hall window the billboard can be seen lit across it.

ties.t: It is the Academy's courtyard.

facts.t: A bell tower of white stone rises over the Academy. Fanny marks it as high ground.

ties.t: It rises over the Academy.

facts.t: Students fight simulated Enders there. A big screen above the pods shows each run.
Inside a pod the hall vanishes, and Fanny stands in a broken street.
After midnight Layla slips in and signs the night log.
A VR drill there copies the Academy grounds.
Layla's grudge kept her there until two in the morning.

ties.t: It is part of the Academy.

facts.t: At a quarter past five each morning Fanny drills alone in its one narrow doorway, blades lit, her back to the dark corridor.
Anything that comes at Fanny in its doorway has to take turns.
At its door Fanny invites Layla to train together.
Late at night a lamp still burns over its one narrow door.
On the tenth morning Layla and Fanny are both there by half past four.
Layla takes Joe's talk of hours to mean the drill hall's sign-in sheets.

ties.t: It is part of the Academy.

facts.t: Three mornings running, Layla lies on the dark gallery above the drill hall while her drone films Fanny.
When Fanny turns toward it, Layla presses her face to the floor.
Fanny tells Layla she can stop watching from the gallery.
Layla says she knows it is cold because she has been lying on it.

ties.t: It runs above the drill hall.

facts.t: At seven Fanny takes the white spiral stair up to class, and Layla races past on the inside.
The next morning Fanny reaches the top a step ahead without knowing it was a race.

ties.t: It leads up to class.

facts.t: Layla sits alone on the sofa by its window, holding down a slat of the blinds to watch the sun set over the city.
After a raid Layla and Fanny share its sofa.
From its window Layla sees the new patch over the Northeastern sector and the first stars.

ties.t: It is the third years' lounge.

facts.t: An abandoned classroom Layla took against the rules.
Her trophy stands on its top shelf, behind spare capacitors.
Layla tells Fanny to meet at the east stairwell at midnight.
It is four flights up in the oldest wing, at the end of a dead-end corridor of stacked desks. The lock on its door is not the Academy's.
Layla calls it her secret base and tells Fanny not to tell anyone.
It smells of solder.
Layla puts Fanny's chocolate box on its top shelf beside the trophy.

ties.t: It is in the Academy's oldest wing.

facts.t: It is long and narrow, with lockers down both walls and a dark doorway at the far end that the practice drones come out of.
It is the only place on school grounds where flying is allowed.

ties.t: It is part of the Academy.

facts.t: After the test match Fanny lies alone on the grass behind the hall.
Birds cross high over it, their shadows sliding across the field.
She stays until the dome's light is the only light left.

ties.t: It lies behind the hall.

facts.t: Layla needles Fanny on the climbing wall, saying someone up there might need carrying.
Fanny reaches the top first, finds nobody and reports it.

ties.t: It is a training ground.

facts.t: Jump training is on the Academy roofs. Layla leaps one gap and scores 10 POINTS.
Fanny swings past on her cables over two gaps to a roof two floors higher.

ties.t: They are the Academy's roofs.

facts.t: Fanny sits alone on the Academy's front steps at night. The stone is cold.

ties.t: They lead into the Academy.

facts.t: Ultra Enders attack the dome over Terrinia's Northeastern sector and rip a breach eight meters by two.
The portal lets out into its smoke, which smells of hot metal and real fire.
On the fifth day of the rebuilding, Fanny and Layla carry panels up the scaffold of one of its ruined buildings.
The new patch of dome over it shines brighter than the rest.

ties.t: It is a sector of Terrinia.

facts.t: At the avenue's end the dome comes down to the ground.
A little girl stands crying in the middle of its pavement.
The gold giant's beam burns a line down it.
Afterward ash lies over it and coats cover some of the shapes along the wall.
That night rescue crews' floodlights go up it in pairs.

ties.t: It runs to the dome in the Northeastern sector.

facts.t: Joe turns the crowd into a side street.
Roger drags Joe toward it.
Fanny sets the girl down behind a van in a side street.
The giant's chest swings toward the side street and the van.
A thin sound comes from it that does not stop.
Fanny sets the rabbit on the broken wall at its mouth.
The thin sound from it has not stopped since dusk.

ties.t: It opens off the avenue.

facts.t: When the Ender heaves, its front comes down in a slab and strikes Joe.
It burns floor by floor after the battle.

ties.t: It stands on the avenue near the breach.

facts.t: Layla runs up its fire stairs three steps at a time to find a line of fire.
From its roof she sees only the Ender's head. A second tower with a glass top floor, and the WELCOME TO TERRINIA billboard, stand between.
Layla fires from its roof through the billboard and both walls of glass into the Ender's core.

ties.t: It stands near the breach.

facts.t: Out on the sand beyond the dome, the gold giant stands up.
All her life Fanny had wanted to see what lay past the dome. It was sand.
The heat cracks her lips.
A swarm comes over the dunes. Out here there is no narrow place to hold.
As the sun sinks the swarm draws back, but most of it is still out there.
The roof has lost its north parapet. Layla sits on the south one with her boots over a two-story drop.
Fanny stands at its broken edge.
Layla drops from its parapet into the dark street, and Fanny jumps after her.

ties.t: It overlooks the dark avenue after the battle.

facts.t: The chapter heading places Oro in another galaxy. Its sky is violet.
Its rulers agree their orders in the Council hall.
Ruby's lesson says Oro's will is Balance.
Ruby's lesson says Oro long ago fought a terrible war with the Enders, and now nobody on Oro may grow strong enough to upset the order.
To Ruby the whole planet is a prison.
Ruby's father says Oro has gone unopposed for thousands of years because its rulers do not bend.
Its violet sky shows through the Gardens' glass.
It is so tall its pillars go up into the dark. Narrow windows run between them, far too high to reach.
Squares of light drift in the air around Ruby.
Oro's rulers agree their orders there.
Ruby's lessons go on there year after year.
Nobody is called to the Council hall to be praised.
Ruby stands in a circle of light on its floor while her father stands outside it.
Its far door opens on white light.

ties.t: It is where Oro's rulers meet.

facts.t: One wall is glass, with only stars behind it.
The Decisionmakers keep Angela hidden there.
Angela stands there on a pedestal counting the stars in the window.
Angela wakes face down on its table, her back panel open.
After each landing its door closes on Angela again.
Ruby falls asleep at her bench there.

ties.t: It is on Oro.

facts.t: Below the Laboratory lies a long hall of tall white windows, where the androids of Project Angel stand in rows.

ties.t: It lies below the Laboratory.

facts.t: It lies behind a plain gray door, with a stream sixty meters off.
It is Ruby's secret base: a stream between two hills under a roof of glass hexagons, with white flowers in the grass.
Sunlight falls through the glass and gives Angela her first warmth.
On the ninth evening Angela sits beside Ruby there.
After her reboot Angela asks whether the Gardens are true.

ties.t: It is on Oro.

facts.t: Angela trains there every day. A Training Droid waits at its far end.
A trainer gives orders from its gallery.
Angela carries a flower through it in her skirt armor.

ties.t: It is on Oro.

facts.t: Ruby told the story of her childhood only once, to the floor of a cell with no window.
Angela remembers a sun rising over a sea, black to gold.
Obsidia's strike came while the humans slept. Most of the dead wore nightclothes.
Obsidia calls the people on the planet the parasites.
Obsidia wants to see what grows in human warmth and human greed.
The Enders came to wipe out humanity and nearly did.
The survivors drew back to Terrinia, humanity's final bastion.
Layla and Fanny call themselves the protectors of all humanity.

ties.t: The Enders came to wipe them out.
The survivors live in Terrinia.

facts.t: Those with enough aspirant power to pilot a suit are called Aspirants.
Selrick Academy was founded to train them.
Half the students wear headgear, which Fanny takes for an Aspirant thing.
The billboard calls Guinevere and Vexana legends even among the Aspirants.
Joe says Aspirants fight in pairs.
Soldiers formed it to fight the Enders and named it for their planet, Dawnbreak.
Fanny's family were Shield soldiers.
It kept Fanny off the front. For two years its soldiers without suits taught her how to hold ground.
Fanny keeps the Shield's hours at the Academy.
With the Shield there had always been somebody to drill with.
Fanny thinks only the Shield's oldest sergeants return their guard to the chin after every punch.
Fanny carries the girl on her left hip, the Shield's way.

ties.t: It is named for the planet Dawnbreak.

facts.t: They were Shield soldiers and trained Fanny from the start.

ties.t: They were Shield soldiers.
They are Fanny's family.

facts.t: They have been scientists for generations. Their message tells Layla: "Second is still wonderful, darling! You're the hope of this family."
At home, talent had been enough for Layla.
Layla says that at home an Ender alert meant the shutters came down and somebody made tea.

ties.t: They are Layla's family.

facts.t: Half the students in the courtyard wear headgear: ears, horns, visors.
Students fight simulated Enders in the VR Battlefield.
They cheer Layla as always No. 1.
After the drill a boy congratulates Layla for finally not trailing in second place.
One day the whole Academy trades chocolate.

ties.t: They study at the Academy.

facts.t: Fanny joins them as a third-year transfer, two years late.
Other third-years laugh down the corridor while Layla sits alone.
The class has been together since first year.
Day after day they go through the gate portal to fight handfuls of Enders.

ties.t: They are a year group of the Academy.

facts.t: When the siren sounds, every tutor is called through the academy gate portal.

ties.t: They teach at the Academy.

facts.t: The Combat Division is the students trained to fight Enders at the front. Joe teaches it.

ties.t: It is a division of the Academy.

facts.t: Joe's team: Layla, Roger and now Fanny.
It drills the Ender weak spot in VR.
Its score: 33 enemies taken out within 10 minutes.
Fanny defeated 15, Roger 2 and Layla 16.
Joe takes Team B3 with him to the breach.
Joe dissolves it.

ties.t: It is a team in Joe's Combat Division class.

facts.t: Joe names Layla and Fanny the Layla-Fanny Team, his and exclusive.
It is not a vote: Aspirants fight in pairs.
They share one score: a kill is a point, a civilian carried clear is ten.
Joe pairs them because they put in the most hours in his year.
On raids Layla takes charge and goes first so Fanny is covered, and Fanny follows with a frown.
Their floodlights go up the dark avenue in pairs and stop at each heap of rubble.
A crew radio says the next block is clear, with nobody left to dig out.

ties.t: They search Terrinia's rubble.

facts.t: Oro's rulers agree their orders in the Council hall.
Nobody is called before it to be praised.
The Project Angel androids are the Council's androids.
Its engineers taught Ruby to program. It orders the heir to build a blade for the Balance Keepers.
Its checkers read what runs in the android, never what sleeps.
Its seal is burned into the plate on every Project Angel body.
Angela is the Council's weapon, built on its order.

ties.t: Its members are Oro's rulers.

facts.t: They give the orders the Council agrees. Ruby's father leads them.
They keep Angela hidden in the Laboratory.
They are Oro's special forces. They go from planet to planet to keep things in "balance."
They want a blade sharper than any they have.
They take Angela from planet to planet in black ships. With her in their ranks they have not lost a landing.

ties.t: They are Oro's special forces.

facts.t: They taught Ruby to program.

ties.t: They are the Council's engineers.

facts.t: They read what ran in an android's mind. They never read what slept.

ties.t: They check work for the Council.

facts.t: They talk two doors away from Angela, and she hears every word.
They say Angela must be kept hidden, or there would be a backlash, and the will of the planet might not like her getting in the way.

ties.t: They work near the Laboratory.

facts.t: A trainer in the gallery orders: "Android Angela. Strike."
They think whatever will not strike can be taught by being hit harder, so they raise the droid's setting.
Angela never tells them she does not want to fight.

ties.t: They watch from the Training Field's gallery.
They train Angela.

facts.t: The mecha suits run on belief. Everyone calls that belief aspirant power.
Those with enough of it to pilot a suit are called Aspirants.
The Chief Combat Instructor says one without the Aspirant spirit is like a gun without bullets.
Joe teaches three ranks: Ultimate Enders, the deadliest, which release the other two; then Super Enders; then plain Enders.
Joe says the small ones kill the most, because there are the most.
None of Joe's three ranks had been gold.
Layla runs through the three ranks when the gold giant appears, and remembers that the siren said Ultra.
Joe teaches that Enders expose their weak spots only when they launch attacks, and that brief moment is all the time you get.
Layla answers that you hit it when it attacks.
Team B3 drills the weak spot in VR.
By Joe's rule the breach Ender's chest opens only when it strikes, so its neck is the only other opening.
Layla applies Joe's rule to the gold giant: its chest opens when it fires.
Joe says that when Enders are hurt badly they go quiet for weeks. This is called a lull, and a lull always ends.
When a boom shakes the hall, Joe says the lull is over.
At sunset the swarm draws back. It has only gone quiet.
Wherever the Storm Citadel's violet storm reaches, human machines die.
After the Citadel climbs away, the street lamps flicker back on.
The recording's caption says the Storm Citadel can unleash devastating electromagnetic interference over large areas.
Interference means every machine under its storm dies.

ties.t: It is the Storm Citadel's weapon.

facts.t: In her assessment Fanny fights the soldiers' way, her back to a narrow alley, so the Enders must come one or two at a time.
Fanny offers to show Layla the alley thing because it saves time.
Fanny drills in the drill hall's one narrow doorway, so anything that comes at her has to take turns.
Layla finds it so simple it makes her angry.
In the test match Layla turns it around: the drones come down one narrow line, so one full charge could take the whole row.
Fanny laughs that Layla did hear her about the alley thing.
Outside the dome there is no narrow place to hold.

ties.t: Fanny fights this way, the soldiers' way she learned with the Shield.

facts.t: Fanny lays Layla flat with her sergeant's throw.
She offers to teach it, saying it saves a lot of time.
Layla had filed the throw, with the promise to teach it, as an insult.

ties.t: It is a throw from Fanny's Shield training.

facts.t: Fanny opens every session with it: "There is no place for mercy on the battlefield."
At first Layla mouths it along, rolling her eyes. By the fifth day she does not.
Fanny says it to Layla while Layla hears the wails from the avenue.
It comes out flat, and Fanny hears how wrong it is.
Fanny thinks she gave Layla the sergeants' line after a hundred and nineteen failures and still has no better one.

ties.t: It is the Shield sergeants' saying.

facts.t: In the test match weapons are set to training power: enough to burst a drone and bruise a girl.
Flying is banned on school grounds, except in the white training corridor.

ties.t: It is an Academy rule.

facts.t: Joe says Aspirants fight in pairs. The suits decided that, not the Academy.
Two who trust each other pull more out of a suit than the same two apart, and nobody has ever explained why.
Joe says Guinevere and Vexana are undefeated and cannot explain why either.
Joe pairs on hours, not scores.
From the day they are paired, Layla and Fanny share one score. A kill is a point. A civilian carried clear is ten.
One score means nobody on the team to beat.
Layla keeps her own score anyway.

ties.t: It is how the team is scored.

facts.t: Layla and Fanny say together: "We've gotta get stronger. After all, we're the protectors of all humanity."
Neither had planned it.

things.name: Heir
aliases: heir to the Decisionmaker of Planet Oro

facts.t: Ruby is the heir to the Decisionmaker of Planet Oro. Heirs can have no friends and no feelings.
Her tutor addresses her as "Heir."
The rule that nobody on Oro may grow strong enough to upset the order includes the heir.
Heirs can have no feelings, but Ruby's tears run anyway.
The Council's order says the heir will build the new blade.
Heirs cannot have friends, so Ruby freezes when Angela calls her one.
Ruby's lesson says everything began with a single burst of chaos, and Balance keeps everything in order now.
The books call Balance the Will of the Cosmos.
Ruby's lesson says Oro's will is Balance too.
The Balance Keepers go from planet to planet to keep things in "balance."
Ruby's lesson says some worlds grow a will of their own as they age, even far ones like Dawnbreak.
The lesson says Oro's will is Balance too.
Oro's technicians say the will of the planet might not like Angela getting in the way.
Ruby tells Angela she does not know what they mean by it and not to say it out loud.
The technicians say that if people saw an android like Angela there would be a backlash.
Ruby explains that a backlash is when people do not like something and do something about it.
In 983, by the prologue's heading, the city's lights go out one street at a time.
The Storm Citadel's violet storm kills every human machine it reaches.
The strike comes after midnight while the humans sleep. Most of the dead wear nightclothes.
Obsidia's Enders walk the ruins.
Obsidia lays the child she made on the scorched ground.
Survivors are laid under a tarp between two broken walls.
When the Storm Citadel leaves, the street lamps flicker back on.
Chapter 1's heading sets the Academy story fourteen years after this night.

ties.t: It happens in Terrinia.

facts.t: The Catastrophe came in 978. In the years after it, the Enders were everywhere.
Fanny's assessment is held in the VR Battlefield.
She pulls a simulated civilian clear first, at a cost of eleven seconds.
She fights with her back to a narrow alley.
Her time, 3:39, goes above Layla's 3:41 on the rankings board.
Layla reruns it five times without saving the civilian. Her best is 3:40.
Layla works out that without the civilian, Fanny did it in 3:28.
Roger says Fanny broke a record nobody had ever broken, on her first day.

ties.t: It takes place in the VR Battlefield.

facts.t: At the week's end Layla and Fanny fight a test match against practice drones in the white training corridor.
A counter over each girl's head shows her kills, and the swarm is shared.
Layla's full-charge shot pulls left past Fanny's shoulder and takes only one drone.
Fanny's counter stops at 0157 and Layla's at 0151.
Fanny later remembers the shot that passed a hand's width from her shoulder.
The last red error line in Layla's log is dated the night of the test match.

ties.t: It takes place in the white training corridor.

facts.t: Joe opens a gold-covered book, and a life-size VR Ender fills the wall.
He teaches that Enders show their weak spots only when they attack.
He teaches the three Ender ranks.
He teaches the lull.
His last slide is the recording of the Storm Citadel.
The VR drill copies the Academy grounds. Fanny blades each Ender's open chest as it strikes, and Layla fires low charge from a doorway.
Roger runs across open ground and an Ender's claw slams down at his heels.
Fanny's cable stops the claw a meter above Roger's face.
Layla's shot passes Fanny's ear into the core.
The shot passed a finger from Roger's face.
Team B3 takes out 33 enemies within 10 minutes.
Layla defeats 16, one more than Fanny. The sixteenth had been on Fanny's cable.

ties.t: It is Team B3's drill.

things.name: the attack on the Northeastern sector

facts.t: A boom shakes the hall, and Joe says the lull is over.
Ultra Enders attack the dome over the Northeastern sector and rip a breach eight meters by two. Every tutor is called through the gate portal.
Joe is struck down by a falling slab while shielding a little girl.
Layla kills the Ender at the breach with one shot through the billboard.
It is the first time Layla and Fanny join forces, and they find they work together well.
Guinevere and Vexana hold the other end of the wall.
A gold giant stands up outside and breaks the dome apart in a ring.
Layla and Fanny destroy the giant together.
They fight back to back in the open, no longer counting kills.
At sunset the swarm draws back. Most of it is still out there.
Ash lies over the avenue, and coats cover some of the shapes along the wall.
Layla's log calls the night before it "the night before the breach."

ties.t: It happens in the Northeastern sector.

facts.t: On a ruined roof the night of the battle, Layla admits Fanny has skill.
Fanny tells Layla about her elder brother, Tigreal.
Layla understands that Fanny was never looking down on her, only past her at her brother.
Layla proposes they get back to training together.
They say together that they must get stronger, because they are the protectors of all humanity.
Every session since the rooftop opens with the sergeants' line.

ties.t: It takes place on the ruined rooftop.

facts.t: On the fifth day of the rebuilding, Fanny and Layla carry panels up the scaffold of a ruined building in the Northeastern sector.
A crew radio says the next block is clear: nobody left to dig out.
As the shift ends, Layla asks Fanny to meet her at midnight.

ties.t: It happens in the Northeastern sector.

facts.t: The whole Academy trades chocolate. Layla carries nineteen boxes.
Fanny has twenty-six boxes stacked behind her.
Fanny gives Layla a pink box with a teal ribbon, for her teammate.
That night Layla puts the box beside her trophy, ribbon facing the room.

ties.t: It happens at the Academy.

facts.t: Ruby's lesson says that long ago Oro fought a terrible war with the Enders. Since then nobody on Oro may grow strong enough to upset the order, and the Enders never came back.

ties.t: It was fought by Oro.

facts.t: The summons comes the morning after Ruby watches the dark ship.
Ruby knows nobody is called to the Council hall to be praised.
Her father rebukes her for laughing alone.
His boot comes down on her tears.
After he leaves, she whispers that she has a plan.

ties.t: It takes place in the Council hall.

facts.t: On the last night a bar crosses the screen beside the chosen name, SUCCESS comes up, and Ruby presses the key.
The android opens her eyes. Every other android woke magenta. Hers are blue.
Ruby names her Angela.
It happened a few weeks before Angela hears the technicians.

ties.t: It happens in the Laboratory.

facts.t: The trainers raise the Training Droid's setting from four to six because Angela will not strike.
A month later the setting is nine, and the fist cracks her shield from edge to edge.
Angela says the warmth is disappearing as she goes down.
She wakes face down on the Laboratory table with her back panel open, and reboots.
Afterward her left shoulder throws blue sparks.

ties.t: It happens on the Training Field.

facts.t: Between training days the Balance Keepers take Angela from planet to planet. With her in their ranks they have not lost a landing.
At each landing she is allowed a ramp's length to look at a strange sky, then the Laboratory door closes again.
After the sixth return Ruby falls asleep at her bench.

ties.t: They are the Balance Keepers' missions.
